text:
mike.support: FYI customer report: Python streaming client (generator) exits after a few tokens, then our app retries and ends up creating duplicate billing events. They attached an app log and minimal repro.

julia.eng: Can you paste the SDK version and a short reproducer? most streaming issues are either SSE delim parsing or a retry/backoff logic bug.

mike.support: Repro from customer:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=\"REDACTED\")
for chunk in client.stream.generate(model=\"open-lite-1\", prompt=\"hi\"):
    print(chunk)
```
They saw the generator yield a couple tokens, then stop (no exception), and after ~2s their wrapper retried the request.

ben.docs: Do they have the client pinned? sometimes v0.4.x had a different heartbeat handling than v0.5.x.

mike.support: They sent pip show:
```
Name: redwood-sdk
Version: 0.4.2
```
Also provided raw stream capture from tcpdump (sanitized).

anna.cust: (pasted sanitized tcpdump)
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream

data: {"delta":"He"}

:data: 

event: heartbeat

data: 

data: {"delta":"llo"}

HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

```

julia.eng: Hmm — two things: 1) older SDK versions treated `:data:` lines (leading colon) differently (docs note changed in v0.5) and 2) the 204 was our keepalive/connection-checker which earlier clients misinterpreted as stream end if it arrives after a partial event. That combination can make the generator finish without raising.

sre-oncall: deploy-bot shows we rolled a change to keepalive midlines last week (rolled 2025-10-12) that switches to `HTTP/204` pings when there's no net data for 1s. Should be safe but older SSE parsers can see it as a disconnect.

mike.support: Customer also reported that their wrapper automatically re-sent the request on generator termination, which caused double token billing. They didn't get an error object from the SDK so their code assumed success and retried.

julia.eng: Action items: 1) confirm SDK behaviour on 0.4.2 w.r.t leading-colon comment lines and 204 handling; 2) add a visible final event or explicit 'end' event so older clients see termination; 3) advise customer to upgrade to 0.5.x which contains SSE parsing fixes.

ben.docs: I'll draft a KB: "Streaming generator exits on interleaved keepalive -> upgrade to 0.5" with repro and mitigation.

mike.support: Quick mitigation for customer: wrap generator with a short guarded wait and raise if it stops producing for >500ms while connection still open. Example:
```python
it = client.stream.generate(...)
last = time.time()
for chunk in it:
    last = time.time()
    handle(chunk)
if time.time() - last < 1.0:
    # suspicious early exit
    raise RuntimeError("stream closed unexpectedly")
```
They said they can patch while updating SDK.

julia.eng: Can anyone attach minimal raw server output to show the 204 arrives between fragments? we need exact framing to write a regression test.

anna.cust: Sent tcpdump as file to Mike.

mike.support: attaching it to the ticket now. Also customer uses a short-lived connection pool which may hide the disconnect timing.

sre-oncall: I'll add a monitoring alert for 204 pings > 0.5s frequency to make sure keepalive behavior is stable.

deploy-bot: build 2025.10.19/sha@abc123 passed CI for sdk 0.5.0.

julia.eng: Next steps:
- Ben: KB + user-facing note (low friction upgrade path)
- SRE: alert + verify no regression from the keepalive change
- Support: provide the customer a signed reproducer and temp mitigation snippet

mike.support: Will send patch snippet and offer to help upgrade. tagging as escalated and assigning to julia for follow-up. :thumbsup:

ben.docs: Drafted KB and PR is up. will link when ready.

julia.eng: Thanks all. we'll add an automated test that injects `HTTP/204` between SSE frames and assert generator yields an error or continues, and include the raw tcpdump as test fixture.

mike.support: Closing loop with customer now, leaving thread open until upgrade confirmed.
